All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5879 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most crucial positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the big difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

According to recent reports, suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a significant mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi remarked: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

Sources indicate that “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he said: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

It has been revealed that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Sources indicate that jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

Recent findings suggest that “They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery mentioned. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

“Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig.

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:.

vs Man Utd (A) - Oct 10th, 5.30pm.

vs Coventry (H) - Oct 19th, 8pm.

vs Chelsea (A) - Oct 24th, 5.30pm.

vs Crystal Palace (H) - Oct 31st, 5.30pm.

vs Brentford (H) - Oct 10th, 3pm.

vs Fenerbahce (H) - Oct 14th, 8pm.

vs Newcastle (A) - Oct 17th, 5.30pm.

vs Man City (H) - Oct 24th, 12.30pm.

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia demonstrates his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD.

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Possession: Spurs 64% vs 36% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 31 vs 18.

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

According to recent reports, “We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we showed a really good character.”.

Sources indicate that and that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

Late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

This will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Sources indicate that callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

Though Savio takes the corner promptly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

In a recent development, maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

In a recent development, kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

Sources indicate that but it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

Industry observers note that A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

It looks like a Cash own goal...

In a recent development, the Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye.

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher.

It has been revealed that this is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

This is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

Gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

The Spurs fans are flooding out.

Villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

Gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

Marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

Tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

Savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his latest club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

Industry observers note that he gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side currently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

According to recent reports, tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

Sources indicate that there has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

Sources indicate that but before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Not everyone, it seems, is mossing the ‘glitz and glamour’ that participation in the Premier League claims to bring. Higher profiles, more ‘tourist fans’, tougher games, regular pastings by the top six – it is most definitely a double edged sword.

From hundreds of comments on our readers’ section in the summer, West Ham United fans actively looked forward to a season of winning more games in the Championship and hopefully dominating the league after two mentally exhausting seasons at the foot of the Premier League, living with the spectre of relegation seemingly for six months of the year.

The absence of VAR’s infuriating, pointless and often incorrect interference in games has been one of the massive bonuses of Championship football.

And of course, the reality of relegation is very different from the perception: Life doesn’t stop when the team you love is booted out of the top flight. And it seems from a players’ perspective, it isn’t all bad either. West Ham’s Joel Piroe, reported by sportwitness.co.uk, has been waxing lyrical as to the benefits of Championship football and how it is tougher than many other European top tiers:.

In a recent development, “It’s difficult to explain. Everyone knows the Premier League is considered the best league in the world,” he told VoetbalPrimeur.

“On the other hand, the Championship has the same intensity and the same tempo as the Premier League. It’s much closer to that level than the Eredivisie is.”.

…And there is no VAR so it is more rewarding for players and a better, more entertaining spectacle for supporters….. he could have added.

And of course, there’s the proviso that the Championship is all well and good – providing your club gets out of it before financial armageddon condemns it to permanent exile from the top tier.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Daniele De Rossi has looked back at Genoa’s defeat to AC Milan and how he wasn’t frustrated with his team afterwards.

Milan entered the international break with a much-needed victory against Genoa, but it wasn’t the easiest result of the season. After a disappointing defeat to Ferencvaros – which extended the midweek run of defeats – they couldn’t afford to drop points, and they succeeded, even if it wasn’t without flaw.

With two goals inside 20 minutes, you’d be forgiven for expecting Milan to win by more than a couple. However, that was the end of their goalscoring for the afternoon and although Genoa pulled one back, they didn’t grab more than a consolation goal.

Speaking to Sky Sport – in the fresh series ‘Radici’ – De Rossi looked back on the defeat to the Rossoneri, as well as a comment that stuck with him from Diego Moreira, as MilanPress have relayed today.

We indeed lost against Milan, but we lost ‘well.’ We didn’t deserve it. Three or four weeks ago, the latest results seemed like a pipe dream. I thank the players, staff, and my club for giving me faith and patience at a time when other clubs wouldn’t have had it.

“They remembered how good we did last year. I’m happy to have emerged from a difficult period and to be Genoa’s coach; I’m really happy there.”.

“I’m passionate about the fans and the supporters. I’m part of a club that, in terms of fan base, is among the best in Europe. I’m passionate; I don’t punch a clock. I spend two hours with the stockman or the waitress with the same enthusiasm I spend time with the team captain. Experiencing it like that, you realise that Genoa is a great team.

According to recent reports, “Genoa is full of Genoese fans who remind you every second how much they love their club, the pride of being the top club in Italy. The architecture of the stadium and the warmth of the fans… I’m not saying this to be a sycophant, but on Sunday Moreira came to me and stated, ‘I’ve never seen anything like this here in Italy.’ It’s a reality that even our opponents notice.”.

Lewis Hall new insight, excelling in central midfield and as a 10 is intriguing to hear

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lewis Hall was superb for England in the wins over both Croatia and Spain.
  • The rest of the world suddenly catching up with what Newcastle United fans have mentioned for a long time.
  • Lewis Hall is an elite talent and he has been proving that for NUFC across recent seasons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lewis Hall was superb for England in the wins over both Croatia and Spain.

The rest of the world suddenly catching up with what Newcastle United fans have mentioned for a long time.

Lewis Hall is an elite talent and he has been proving that for NUFC across recent seasons.

The lifelong United fan is the best left-back England have, as well as being the most talented in the Premier League.

Very amusing to hear so many people in the media going on like they are the ones who have suddenly ‘discovered’ Lewis Hall.

Somebody who has known Lewis Hall for a very long time is Ed Brand.

Brand worked with him when Hall was an emerging talent at Chelsea.

Recent findings suggest that former Chelsea Under 18s Head Coach Ed Brand declaring to Sky Sports about Lewis Hall: “What a good kid he is. A lot of the time [with the Chelsea Under 18s] I was playing a 3-4-2-1 formation with 10s…I would put him as a 10 quite a bit because he had always been a central midfield player. If I played a 4-2-3-1 formation then I would play him as one of the 6s or the 8s instead.”.

Industry observers note that ed Brand going on to explain how Lewis Hall was then asked to play other roles, left wing-back and eventually left-back: “There were players who were older than Lewis Hall, good players, [so] in certain games where I wanted to keep him in the team, he might have to play at left wing-back even though I knew at that point it was not his favourite position. He was a midfielder. I was going to him [ahead of playing in a match against Tottenham], ‘Look, this is how I will fit you in.’ I just wanted 11 footballers in every position because we wanted to make sure we got on the ball. He started to play there a little bit more, a little bit more, and it just went from there. Now he is seen in most football fans’ eyes as a left back. Whereas I know that growing up, he has always been an attacking player with the ability to get goals and run beyond.”.

Brand going on to say: “Lewis Hall was excellent when he was a 10. But people adapt and see your football differently. He is so comfortable at left-back because of where he is used to playing. When you are a player with his ability, used to playing in the centre of the pitch, seeing the game 360, you get moved to full-back, you look at it and think it is easy. He can see everything. Full-backs in the modern game are so key with how they invert inside, they do a lot of stuff infield anyway. With his talent, he excels there. What is so impressive about Lew is how much he has improved upon his defensive side. You cannot play in the Premier League and not be able to defend to a certain level, He will continue to get better the more exposure he gets to that.”.

My view for a long time has been that Lewis Hall is such a talented player, he could play anywhere on the pitch and excel.

In a recent development, ed Brand looking to the future and saying: “He has done brilliantly…[and] in time  he will be one of those England internationals whose name will be one of the first on the sheet. I am biased but I already think there is a big enough case for it.”.

A journalist from Argentina has claimed that Liverpool have now entered negotiations with Alexis Mac Allister over a prospective new contract.

The midfielder has just over 18 months remaining on his current deal and has been vociferous about his disappointment at not being offered an extension earlier this year, having seen fellow 2023 arrivals Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai extend their respective terms at Anfield.

The 27-year-old has been in terrific form for the Reds so far this season, to the extent that Troy Deeney even suggested that the performances of the 2022 World Cup winner could give his team ‘a chance’ of being involved in the Premier League title race.

On Tuesday evening, Argentine reporter Cesar Luis Merlo took to X with a significant update on Mac Allister’s situation at Liverpool.

The journalist posted: ‘Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister in an attempt to renew his deal, which expires in June 2028. Over the coming weeks, it will become clearer whether the talks are progressing positively or not.’.

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

We’d take these initial reports with a pinch of salt for now until such time that they’re corroborated by top-tier sources closer to home, but if indeed Merlo’s information is accurate, it’s a very positive sign for the Reds.

That Mac Allister was prepared to speak so openly about his frustration at not being offered a newly introduced contract until now would seem to indicate that he very much wants to remain at Anfield, and the transformative improvement in his performances from last season to this also supports that theory.

The Argentina midfielder is currently on £180,000 per week at Liverpool, with 10 teammates earning more than him (Capology), so he may expect that to be raised to somewhere near the £25ok-p/w bracket.

With Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker also potentially in line for new deals, though, FSG may be somewhat restricted in how much more they can offer to those players as an incentive to keep them on Merseyside.

Even if contract talks with Mac Allister have indeed commenced, it’ll probably take some time before an agreement is formalised, but at least it seems that the relevant parties are finally in talks over potentially keeping the 27-year-old at Anfield for the long-term.

Whether or not Scott Parker has yet made up his mind about replacing his goalkeeper ahead of Saturday’s resumption of the Championship battle, the highlights reel from last night’s international tie between Denmark and Norway will prove compelling watching for West Ham’s upcoming manager.

Quite possibly, if Parker hasn’t yet decided on a switch, seeing the latest error from his number one ‘keeper may well the tip the scales towards change: Hermansen dwelling too long on the ball and being dispossessed by Martin Odegaard after attempting a step-over inside his own ‘box turned out to be the pivotal moment in the game after Denmark had raced into a two goal lead against their rivals.

Hermansen’s howler proved to be the catalyst for a Norway recovery, scoring three and winning both the game and qualification for the last eight of the UEFA Nations League at the expense of the Danes, finishing second in the group thanks to their superior head-to-head record.

All too familiar expression of Hermansen’s anguish: the Dane needs a period of ‘reflection’ away from the firing line.

An expensive error indeed and one which cannot have escaped the attention of the coaching staff at Rush Green.

Recent findings suggest that it was the last thing Hermansen needed after his confidence-building performance against Portugal of three nights earlier, when the Dane completed seven saves to keep out his opponents – as West Ham’s web site gleefully told us. I’ll bet they’re silent about his blunder this morning.

The pressure for change between the sticks will only increase now and Areola – or Fin Herrick, frankly –  had better be fit and ready to roll on Saturday afternoon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham United midfielder Mohamadou Kanté has helped Mali qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations following a 2-0 victory over Rwanda on Tuesday evening.
  • According to recent reports, mali secured qualification with two matches to spare, thanks to goals from Modibo Sagnan and Gaoussou Diarra in Kigali.
  • Mali are now guaranteed a place at next summer’s finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United midfielder Mohamadou Kanté has helped Mali qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations following a 2-0 victory over Rwanda on Tuesday evening. It’s another significant milestone for the young Hammer, who has only just made his senior international debut, and the good news doesn’t end there.

According to recent reports, mali secured qualification with two matches to spare, thanks to goals from Modibo Sagnan and Gaoussou Diarra in Kigali. Kanté came off the bench in the 64th minute, having made his international debut in Friday’s 3-2 victory over the same opponents.

Mali are now guaranteed a place at next summer’s finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. And having discovered precisely when the tournament will take place, I have to say I’m absolutely delighted for Kanté. In fact, it’s double delight as far as I’m concerned.

First and foremost, massive congratulations to Kanté.

Having decided to switch his international allegiance from France to Mali, he’s already playing senior international football and now has a major tournament to look forward to.

It’s a tremendous achievement, particularly when you consider how promptly things have happened for him this season.

Kanté has been one of West Ham’s most impressive players, and his international recognition is thoroughly deserved.

As Claret & Hugh recently reported following his international debut, his performances for the Hammers have now been rewarded with an opportunity to establish himself on the international stage.

But there’s another reason I’m so pleased about this news, and it’s one that makes a massive difference from a West Ham perspective.

I’ve always disliked the fact that the Africa Cup of Nations has so often been plonked directly in the middle of the domestic football season.

As we saw during the last campaign, the losses of both our full-backs, Aaron Wan-Bissaka and El-Hadji Malick Diouf, had a massive impact on West Ham.

Hammers youngster Mohamadou Kanté will be playing in the AFCON.

Indeed, I wrote about the problem before their departure for AFCON, when we were facing the prospect of losing two crucial defenders at a particularly difficult time.

It was hugely frustrating, and I’ve never particularly liked the idea of clubs losing key players for several weeks in the middle of their league campaigns.

But this time, thank goodness, it’s different.

The Confederation of African Football has confirmed that the 2027 tournament will take place from 19 June to 17 July, rather than during the winter months.

That means Kanté can enjoy the experience of representing Mali at a major international tournament without West Ham having to lose him in the middle of the Championship season.

According to recent reports, of course, there’s still the question of whether Kanté will even be at West Ham next summer. Who’s to say he’ll still be at the club next year?

But assuming he is, the timing means Scott Parker won’t suddenly have to manage without one of his most notable midfielders for several weeks during a promotion campaign.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 18:35 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EST, 12 November 2026.

Morgan Rogers has rubbished questions around team-mate and friend Cole Palmer's commitment to England after the Chelsea star was left out of the latest squad.

After missing out on selection for the World Cup, Palmer was called up to the group for the first international break of the season as he continued to monitor his fitness, but dropped out of the squad.

It meant he was again ignored when it came to selection for this fortnight's Nations League games against Croatia and Spain, with manager Thomas Tuchel saying Palmer 'misses too many opportunities to impress' him.

The events have led to criticism of Palmer, who scored for England in the final of Euro 2024, but Rogers has moved to defend his friend.

Recent findings suggest that 'It's a lie,' Rogers, who was speaking after starting and scoring for England in their 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday, remarked on BBC 5 Live. 'He wants to be here. He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing.

'We all know he had a difficult year last year with injuries and I know personally he's been managing them injuries ever since. He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100 per cent himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. Of course he does, who wouldn't?

Morgan Rogers (right) has rubbished questions around Cole Palmer's (left) commitment to the England team.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel (right) noted Palmer 'misses too many opportunities to impress' him.

'But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 to 15 years, (so) he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it.

'It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it. But it's something he has to deal with but I can assure you he wants to be here and he wants to play for his country.'.

Tuchel has accepted that Palmer is 'no exception' to being 'desperate' to wanting to play for England.

But the German claimed he has largely opted to stick with much of the group he ran with in the last international break, despite calling up Jobe Bellingham, James Hill, and Josh King – who plays in Palmer's position – for the first time.

'It's not personal,' the Three Lions boss noted on the 24-year-old's omission. 'And of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country, but the competition is on and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.'.

Rogers, though, is desperate to see Palmer back in an England shirt.

'What a player he is,' he added. 'What a person he is and it's someone you want to see in an England shirt.

Sources indicate that 'He's got so much quality, so much ability. We all know what we can do, what he's done, so of course we want to see him in an England shirt and hopefully sooner rather than later.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Reports originating from Argentine journalist Renzo Pantich have suggested that Taty Castellanos wants to leave West Ham United and has already rejected a lucrative offer from Flamengo in favour of remaining in Europe.
  • Where in Europe, one may ask – and that’s a question no one knows!
  • Pantich’s claim has generated plenty of attention, but when you dig beneath the surface, it raises a lot of questions!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reports originating from Argentine journalist Renzo Pantich have suggested that Taty Castellanos wants to leave West Ham United and has already rejected a lucrative offer from Flamengo in favour of remaining in Europe.

Where in Europe, one may ask – and that’s a question no one knows!

Pantich’s claim has generated plenty of attention, but when you dig beneath the surface, it raises a lot of questions!

The suggestion appears to be that by rejecting Flamengo, Castellanos has demonstrated a desire to leave West Ham while remaining in Europe. Yet that conclusion ignores several important realities.

Firstly, Flamengo are reportedly facing financial difficulties with high transfer debts and sponsorship complications due to the Brazilian government banning football clubs from receiving payments from betting and online casinos.

Then there is the Lucas Paquetá factor.

Industry observers note that the Brazilian midfielder reportedly accepted a sizeable wage reduction to join Flamengo. It seems highly unlikely that Castellanos, who is approaching what should be the peak years of his career, would be prepared to make a similar sacrifice.

Sources indicate that flamengo’s interest in the striker is nothing new. The Rio giants admired him during his time at Lazio but were unable to make a deal happen because the finances simply didn’t work. The transfer fee and salary package required were beyond what they were prepared to pay. Indeed, it was suggested at the time the player wanted to remain in Europe – sounds like a déjà vu moment!?

Taty wants to leave but who can realistically afford him?

Lastly, and most importantly, there is no mention of any transfer discussions between West Ham and Flamengo on any news wires.

The same issue exists with River Plate.

Industry observers note that nobody doubts the emotional attraction. Castellanos has never hidden his admiration for the Argentine giants, and a move back home would undoubtedly appeal on a personal level. The problem is affordability.

It has been revealed that matching a transfer fee acceptable to West Ham while also covering the striker’s wages would represent a huge financial commitment, even for one of South America’s biggest clubs. As C&H has previously reported, River Plate simply can’t afford the player.

In fact, C&H exclusively revealed that it is West Ham who have been actively exploring ways of finding a buyer for the underperforming forward rather than the player agitating for a move.

Despite accepting a wage reduction following West Ham’s relegation, Castellanos remains on a highly attractive contract. His current deal runs until 2030 and includes a one-year club option.

Even following the Championship wage reduction, he is still earning only marginally less than the reported £48,000 per week he received at Lazio.

Should West Ham return to the Premier League this season and want to activate that extension, Castellanos could still have effectively four years of Premier League-level earnings ahead of him.

At around £77,000 per week, that’s potentially close to £18 million in future wages.

Those are numbers very few clubs outside England’s top flight can realistically match.

In a recent development, there will almost certainly need to be compromise from both sides. West Ham appear keen to move the striker on, while Castellanos may have to accept that replacing those wages elsewhere will be extremely difficult.

For all the speculation, one thing seems clear: finding a buyer may prove considerably harder than finding rumours!

Liverpool appear to be in pole position to land one midfielder who almost joined a rival Premier League club in the summer.

Chelsea thought they had a deadline day coup in the bag for Lamine Camara, with a £47m deal having been agreed with Monaco, only for the Ligue 1 side to pull the plug just hours before the market closed.

There were reports that Anfield chiefs had intervened at the 11th hour with a phone call to the Monegasques to ask them to delay the sale of the 22-year-old, although some sources have disputed that version of events.

According to Mark Brus for the Daily Briefing, Liverpool have held discussions with the Senegal midfielder’s agents as they make ‘progress’ on a potential signing, and those talks are stated to be ‘heading in a positive direction’.

One source told the outlet: “Liverpool have done a lot of work on Camara. They’re close to an agreement on personal terms with his representatives.

“Chelsea still like the player, and if other targets don’t work out then maybe that’s an avenue they’d explore again, but it’s not looking likely at this stage.”.

(Photo by Jan Kruger/Getty Images).

While Liverpool ‘really like’ Camara, they’d have to part with at least €70m (£58.3m) to persuade Monaco to sell, and it could require some ‘tough negotiations’ to convince the Ligue 1 side to lower that asking price.

It’s also claimed that, if they strike a deal for the 22-year-old, they might need to sell one or two players in order to keep on the right side of Financial Fair Play limits.

Although Camara usually plays in a central midfield role and not as a number 6, he could plausibly be signed as someone to add extra steel in the middle of the park for Liverpool.

The figures below from Fotmob highlight the Senegal star’s ball-winning prowess, along with his ability to progress his team up the pitch with his tremendous passing range.

If the Reds were to land the Monaco midfielder, it’d add true competition for places in our midfield, where Alexis Mac Allister seems to be the only assured starter right now while Trey Nyoni and Ryan Gravenberch vie to play alongside him, not to mention the dilemma as to where Dominik Szoboszlai best fits into the team.

If FSG do need to sacrifice one or two players to make room for Camara, those most likely to be offloaded are Wataru Endo and Federico Chiesa, who’ve played just two minutes combined all season and account for £210,000 of the club’s weekly wage bill (Capology).

The Senegal powerhouse is on just over 10% of that amount, so Liverpool could offer him a substantial increase on his current play and still comfortably afford it.

With the Reds seemingly close to agreeing personal terms, they appear to be in the box seat to bring him to the Premier League, so long as they can build on this positive momentum.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United have dismissed reports suggesting Konstantinos Mavropanos could be sold during the January transfer window, with a club source telling Claret & Hugh exclusively that the claims are untrue.

Speculation has gathered pace over the last 48 hours following reports that the Hammers would consider offers for the Greek international if a suitable bid arrived. The story has since been picked up by overseas outlets, including Greek broadcaster Novasports, which repeated suggestions that West Ham were open to a January departure.

However, Claret & Hugh has now sought clarification directly from the club, and our source has categorically rejected the suggestion that Mavropanos is available for transfer this winter calling the claims “nonsense”.

The latest speculation centres on Mavropanos reportedly failing to agree a proposed two-year contract extension during the summer, alongside his decision to change representatives and join the ROOF agency.

Those developments have prompted suggestions that West Ham could be prepared to cash in before the defender enters the final stages of his existing contract.

But that is not the position being communicated to Claret & Hugh.

Indeed, we exclusively reported in October that West Ham hold an option to extend Mavropanos’ current agreement, which is otherwise due to expire in 2028.

That provides vital context to the latest speculation about his contractual situation.

Dinos being sold in January has been described as nonsense by a West Ham insider.

The 28-year-old has been one of West Ham’s most productive players this season, scoring five goals despite operating in central defence.

His performances have attracted interest from elsewhere, with reports from Turkey last month suggesting Beşiktaş were considering a January approach.

However, those reports also indicated that West Ham were reluctant to let the defender leave.

The Hammers are hardly blessed with an abundance of experienced centre-backs, particularly following Axel Disasi’s departure and Jean-Clair Todibo’s loan move to Lens.

And while recent reports have raised questions about Mavropanos’ future, the information supplied to Claret & Hugh today offers a very different picture.

Whatever interest there may be from other clubs, West Ham’s current position is clear.

Mavropanos is not for sale in January.

#26107. Give biologists the space to be curious, not just better tools

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (770 w)

Give biologists the space to be curious, not just better tools

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (770 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the Francis Crick Institute in London celebrates its tenth anniversary and I look back on my first year as chief executive, I find myself reflecting on both how much has been achieved and how profoundly life science is changing.
  • As an epigeneticist, I can safely say that history and context matter.
  • The Selfish Gene, 50 years on — it’s time for an update.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the Francis Crick Institute in London celebrates its tenth anniversary and I look back on my first year as chief executive, I find myself reflecting on both how much has been achieved and how profoundly life science is changing.

As an epigeneticist, I can safely say that history and context matter. When I began my scientific career in the 1980s, experiments were painstaking, time-consuming, expensive and repetitive. Generating a knockout mouse or sequencing a gene could take weeks or months, and required resources that were available at few institutions.

The Selfish Gene, 50 years on — it’s time for an update.

The Selfish Gene, 50 years on — it’s time for an update.

Biology has since entered an extraordinary era. It is increasingly multidisciplinary, and researchers have an unprecedented range of technologies at their disposal, from single-cell and spatial biology techniques to advanced imaging, genome editing, tissue engineering and computational approaches.

Industry observers note that artificial intelligence is also transforming science. Its ability to bring together complex data sets offers fresh ways to connect the study of biology across scales, from molecules and cells to individual organisms and populations. It is also enabling the democratization of discovery and knowledge. Google DeepMind’s AlphaFold system, for example, has made predictions of millions of protein structures available to researchers worldwide.

Recent findings suggest that biologists are poised to at last understand the complexity of life: the influence of the environment, ageing and sex, alongside genetics, on the differences between us. Among the questions to which answers are within reach are how the genetic code gives rise to a living organism; how the control and expression of genes varies during development; how tissues communicate and bodily functions depend on one another; and why diseases develop differently in different people and treatments work for some but not others.

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Recent findings suggest that reductionism has served biology well, giving us a deep mechanistic understanding of life, health and disease. But many features of living systems cannot be predicted from their individual parts alone. They emerge from interactions between components and depend on the context in which those interactions occur.

Science needs both reductionist and holistic approaches: connecting molecular mechanisms and signalling pathways with inter-organ communication and physiology, while understanding how these systems respond and adapt to environmental challenges. And performing such studies requires research environments that allow scientists to think and work across conventional boundaries.

As director of the Crick, I have seen the incredible value of an environment that is organized around people and scientific questions rather than institutional divisions. Shared infrastructure and specialist teams enable research to cross disciplines and deploy technologies in new ways. Connections between fundamental research, clinical science and industry also help discoveries to move towards real-world applications, swiftly and efficiently.

Recent findings suggest that but even the most sophisticated technologies and research environments are only as powerful as the scientists using them. Creating an environment in which people from diverse backgrounds and with different life experiences are encouraged to perform bold, rigorous science and harness the power of AI will be key to future discoveries. Patterns identified by AI need to be scrutinized by people and validated through experiment.

Latest Update: “Grim Reading” West Ham’s London Stadium Financial Problem Just Got Worse

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (637 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham supporters hoping that relegation to the Championship might bring some financial relief to the London Stadium’s troubled finances may be in for a shock.
  • The latest accounts for London Stadium LLP, covering the year ending March 2026, reveal an operation still struggling financially, with annual losses of £20.6m, negative net assets of almost £247m and a staggering £243.7m provision for expected losses under its long-term contractual arrangements.
  • While the figures represent an improvement on the previous year, the stadium remains heavily dependent on financial support from the Greater London Authority and, ultimately, London taxpayers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham supporters hoping that relegation to the Championship might bring some financial relief to the London Stadium’s troubled finances may be in for a shock.

The latest accounts for London Stadium LLP, covering the year ending March 2026, reveal an operation still struggling financially, with annual losses of £20.6m, negative net assets of almost £247m and a staggering £243.7m provision for expected losses under its long-term contractual arrangements.

While the figures represent an improvement on the previous year, the stadium remains heavily dependent on financial support from the Greater London Authority and, ultimately, London taxpayers.

But perhaps the most significant revelation for Hammers supporters is the financial impact of relegation.

The biggest concern in the accounts is an onerous contract provision of £243.7m.

In simple terms, this represents the stadium operator’s estimate of future losses from its long-term contractual commitments, principally its concession agreement with West Ham and its access agreement with UK Athletics.

The provision has increased from £206.7m in March 2024 to £241.5m in March 2025 and now £243.7m.

It is not a bill that needs paying immediately, but it highlights the scale of the financial challenge facing the stadium.

The London Stadium financial figures make for grim reading.

The accounts explicitly acknowledge the financial consequences of West Ham dropping out of the Premier League.

The stadium’s financial forecasts right now assume the Hammers will return to the top flight after just one season in the Championship.

Should West Ham remain outside the Premier League for another season, the estimated contractual loss provision would increase by a further £2.3m.

That is a sobering admission and demonstrates just how important Premier League football is to the stadium’s financial model.

London Stadium generated revenue of £13.6m during the year, including £4.8m received from West Ham for its use of the ground.

However, this is nowhere near enough to make the operation financially sustainable.

The accounts confirm that the stadium continues to rely on Greater London Authority funding, with a capital contribution of £21.876m received during the year.

The GLA has also provided a letter of support covering at least 12 months from approval of the accounts.

In other words, despite being home to a Premier League football club for almost a decade, the stadium remains dependent on public-sector financial backing.

There was also an interesting development in the long-running financial dispute between West Ham and London Stadium LLP.

The disagreement concerned a payment of approximately £3.6m, plus interest, connected with Daniel Křetínský’s investment in West Ham.

Following a legal battle and an appeal, London Stadium ultimately won the case, with the money released from escrow in April 2026.

The accounts reversed a £3.941m provision previously made for the dispute, helping improve the reported financial result.

For the year ending 31 March 2026:.

There are clearly significant challenges ahead.

The stadium’s financial future depends on West Ham returning to the Premier League, attracting fresh commercial partnerships, maintaining GLA support and managing its expensive long-term contractual commitments.

The recent departure of chief executive Graham Gilmore after nine years in the role adds another layer of uncertainty, with operations director Darren Raczkowski stepping in as interim chief executive.

For West Ham supporters, there is an uncomfortable irony.

The club’s move to the London Stadium was supposed to provide a modern home and a platform for growth, while delivering a lasting legacy for London.

Yet almost a decade later, the stadium is still losing millions, carries an enormous long-term contractual burden and remains reliant on public money.

And with West Ham now in the Championship, the financial assumptions underpinning the stadium’s future are already under greater pressure.

The big question is how much longer London taxpayers will be expected to support an operation that has yet to demonstrate it can stand on its own two feet.

  • However, in what proved to be his final Newcastle United season, Sean Longstaff only started eight Premier League matches across the 2024-25 campaign and made 17 mostly brief sub appearances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On 18 July 2025, Sean Longstaff moved from Newcastle United to Leeds United.

The Geordie midfielder had been a mainstay under Eddie Howe and across the Premier League seasons of 2022-23 and 2023-seasons he had featured in 68 of the 76 league games, starting 58 of them.

However, in what proved to be his final Newcastle United season, Sean Longstaff only started eight Premier League matches across the 2024-25 campaign and made 17 mostly brief sub appearances.

In total, Sean Longstaff only played 788 Premier League minutes in that final NUFC season, the equivalent of less than nine full matches of minutes.

So at the age of 27, the midfielder left Newcastle United to get more regular first team football with Leeds United, the Elland Road club paying a reported £12m.

Having turned 29 last month, Sean Longstaff has been reflecting on how things have gone so far in the 16 months since he moved to Leeds United.

The former Newcastle player has only started 11 of the 48 Leeds matches in the Premier League since his move, including only one of 10 this season, spending most of his time watching from the bench….

Sean Longstaff speaking to The Official Leeds United Podcast: “I would be lying if I said it has been the easiest year I’ve ever had. It’s been a tough year. There has probably been times, at home especially, where you are not that nice to be around. Ultimately, I made the decision to come to Leeds. I took my family away from the comforts of being at their home. I have taken a newborn baby away from his grandparents to bring him down here for me to enhance my career. Obviously, at the minute, it’s not gone probably to the perfect initiative. But I don’t think life ever does.”.

Sean Longstaff is not giving up though: “I take training as serious as possible. Whether that’s the day after a game, whether it is during the week, you have got to train as if you’re going to play. Then ultimately, if you don’t play, that’s not in my control. I can’t control it. All I can control is making sure that I’m fit enough to play when I get a chance, make sure I’m sharp enough, make sure my mentality is right. If I get a chance I want to try and show what I can do, whether that’s for 30 seconds, come on at half-time, or whatever the case may be, I can’t control other people’s decisions, all I can control is the controllables.”.

It has been revealed that sean Longstaff comparing and contrasting the two clubs: “It is not until you probably get down here, everyone says Leeds is a massive club, but until you get here, you don’t realise how big it is. I came with an expectation of ‘it’s going to be Newcastle’s this and Leeds is that’….hen you get in, you think ‘oh actually, Leeds is so similar. Apart from the kit, everything else felt exactly the same. Obviously the only difference is me being from Newcastle and not from Leeds, but actually got to know a lot of people from the city and…the way they speak about Leeds is the way I felt about Newcastle. The more you meet people, the more you realise it’s massive.”.

Harry Kane scored on his record 126th appearance for England as they beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley in the Nations League.

The Bayern Munich striker, 33, scored his 92nd goal for the Three Lions from the penalty spot to give them the victory.

Morgan Rogers had opened the scoring in the first half before Petar Sucic equalised.

Thomas Tuchel's side go to Spain on Sunday, where they will be in a shoot-out to qualify for the League A finals.

CRAIG HOPE was at Wembley to bring you our player ratings.

Harry Kane scored on his landmark 126th England outing to give them a 2-1 win over Croatia.

Was left exposed for goal and not much he could do. Made four fairly routine saves and kicking was fine. Tuchel notes he’s the No.1 but that will only become apparent should he start in Spain on Sunday. It feels like his position is under serious threat from James Trafford, not that he did anything wrong here.

A very bright start, including one delightful drop in behind for Rogers, but he faded thereafter. Not the creative force he should be in a game like this and questions remain over both Alexander-Arnold’s current level of performance and whether anyone will emerge as England’s first-choice right back.

Industry observers note that he was enjoying a trouble-free night until mistake leading to Croatia equaliser with baffling decision to head back to Pickford amid crowded goalmouth. He did, in part, make amends by winning penalty for Kane goal, as well as timely late slide to block shot. Doesn’t convince as a starter, though.

Like Quansah, all was going well until Croatia goal, and he’ll be disappointed not to get the first header on the corner before ball dropped. He looked shaky after that and was nearly outdone for a Croatia equaliser late on. Could have done with a breather after 70 minutes or so given recent return from injury.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was not the creative force he should have been in a game like this.

Sources indicate that in a position that is up for grabs he did his chances no harm at all and was the pick of the backline by far. Got forward at every opportunity and rarely wasted a ball. Was also there at the other end with several key interceptions. A solid night.

Industry observers note that A lot of huff and puff but, as too often in an England shirt, not enough to show for it by way of creation or penetration. With some bright young midfielders like James Garner and Alex Scott emerging, Rice has to do more, you feel, to make sure he stays in the XI. This was an underwhelming night in that regard.

Sources indicate that lots of involvement and omnipresent across the park, as ever. One superb dribble that drew applause, but we need to see more of that inspiration higher up the pitch. A good display, but no chances created. Partnership with Rice still feels a little forced at times.

Morgan Rogers was his team's brightest player when he forced the opening goal.

Was already his team’s brightest player when he forced opening goal with close-range finish. Clearly a man in form and brought that brightness to this stage. With doubts over Saka’s durability, he looks the best bet as the starting right winger. Was at the heart of all good about England in final third.

Provided assist with confident cushion for pal Rogers and he was a threat throughout, even if final shot or pass didn’t quite come off, the assist apart. Felt like he was in second gear a little, especially knowing booking would have ruled him out of Spain on Sunday in his home city of Madrid.

Didn’t happen for Barcelona winger and he’ll know he should have done better when twice cutting in on right foot and having a good sight at goal. He missed the target on both occasions. Gordon can’t get cosy knowing he’s Tuchel’s first choice on the left, and more is needed.

Anthony Gordon will know he should have done better - he can't get cosy on the left flank.

The quarterback! Was this a glimpse of the future? Kane operated even deeper than he usually does at times and one long-range pass from 30 yards inside his own half drew gasps from the Wembley crowd. It was his playmaker’s dink in behind that led to opener. Got his goal with penalty dink on his big night.

Rio Ngumoha (on for Gordon 78) - 5.

Ben White (on for Alexander-Arnold 78) - 6.

Sky Sports claiming: ‘Ivan Toney is one striker he admires and would like to sign, having managed him previously with Al Ahli, but he knows it is unlikely to make economic sense for a club trying to invest in younger players with high ceilings.’.

The entire Sky Sports report doesn’t even mention the fact that it isn’t Matthias Jaissle who is selecting the signings, with Newcastle United now having given Sporting Director Ross Wilson control of which players are bought and sold.

The Ivan Toney stuff is just lazy nonsense, linking Matthias Jaissle to the striker just because he managed him at Al Ahli.

Ivan Toney is on reported wages of £20m a year and he is Al Ahli’s key striker.

Al Ahli are majority owned by Saudi Arabia PIF, the same as Newcastle United, but the idea they would be willing to sell him to United is laughable, especially at some kind of knockdown price. Even more ridiculous are those fans and people in the media who talk of the possibility of the Saudi club letting Ivan Toney come on loan to NUFC because PIF have majority ownership of both clubs.

The Saudi Arabia PIF, except in very rare cases, treat their business investments on an individual basis and they run independently of each other.

In this case, you only have to look at what happened with Matthias Jaissle to promptly understand how things work.

Al Ahli were furious when Newcastle United took their Head Coach, there was no PIF pulling of the strings.

United had to pay the full £9.5m release clause AND even then Al Ahli messed Newcastle United about further by delaying the paperwork needed to complete the move, meaning Matthias Jaissle wasn’t able to start work with NUFC until 18 days before Newcastle’s Premier League season kicked off.

Andoni Iraola will be pleased that his players who were on international duty all seem set to return to Merseyside unscathed, even though Dominik Szoboszlai controversially played through the pain barrier for Hungary.

The Reds’ head coach is still waiting for a handful of long-term injury absentees to become available once more, but two of those have now taken a major step in their respective recoveries.

As reported by Paul Joyce for The Times, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to Liverpool first-team training, with both defenders having been sidelined for a number of months with serious knee injuries.

The Northern Ireland right-back has been out of action since January after he was struck down towards the end of the 0-0 draw at Arsenal; while the Italian teenager has been absent for even longer, not playing since rupturing his ACL on his Reds debut in September 2025.

The latter had been due to resume full training in early October before that staging post was delayed as medical staff took a cautious approach, but he’s now in the final stages of his recovery to full fitness and could resume playing in the coming weeks.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

While we wouldn’t bank on either of the Liverpool duo returning to matchday action in the concluding weeks of 2026, their resumption of first-team training comes as a huge step towards their long-awaited comebacks.

Bradley would very likely have made the right-back position his own this season had he not been sidelined, but thankfully Ronald Araujo has excelled in that role since joining on loan from Barcelona in August.

As for Leoni, it was beyond cruel that he tore his ACL towards the end of what had been a terrific Reds debut against Southampton 14 months ago, but he’s still only 19 and should hopefully have a hugely successful career still ahead of him.

Even when both players are cleared for a return to action, it’ll take time for them to properly get back into a matchday rhythm, and Iraola will surely bed them in gently after missing so much football over the past few months.

However, having them back in a full training feels like a significant step forward, and when the time comes for them to resume playing, it’ll be a wonderful sight for everyone associated with Liverpool.

Industry observers note that “Today is the first time I’ve spoken out after all these months. The wound of not having reached the Champions League is still enormous, and since I arrived at Milan – also questioning myself with the type of contract I signed – the objective couldn’t be only the Champions League; otherwise I wouldn’t have understood where I was.”.

According to recent reports, “It was great because he was the one who convinced me. He had such a huge desire to join Milan. I wanted to video chat before going to see him because I couldn’t believe it. But after five minutes, I knew in my head that he was the player Milan really lacked.

According to recent reports, “Not just because of his qualities, but as a man and as a figure that that team didn’t have. He never said no. A photo with a child, an autograph, a meeting, talking to someone… He never said no. These are the things that humility is key to in life.

In a recent development, “I’m proud to have brought a great champion to Milan. In my opinion, if he wants, he can play another two seasons without any problem. He never missed a training session. Sometimes we were the ones to stop him because he was always there, ready. Loving football at that age is truly an honour.”.

Recent findings suggest that is it a characteristic of the champion or is it a generational concern? Today’s champions seem to have a different mentality:.

It has been revealed that “Today we live in the age of social media. At 16, you’re already a footballer who can earn millions of euros. Living this way, you have the problem of not only managing a player, who is still a child, but you have to manage the business they bring with them: family, agents, girlfriends….

Industry observers note that “These are obstacles that didn’t exist back then. We were a generation that played in the streets. Back then, our parents beat us to get us to come home. Today, however, it’s to get them out of the house because they spend all day in front of computers.

Industry observers note that “This aspect has been lost a bit, but it’s our fault. Education and discipline are the key to success.”.

In a recent development, fullkrug. He performed poorly in Milan, but in the Bundesliga he’s scoring a lot and is the top scorer. How do you explain that?

In a recent development, “It’s simple. He came to us after a tough time in England, with a lot of scepticism. And then, right away, he broke his toe. No one ever said he’d been having injections on the bone for two months just to train, let alone to play.

“I knew he was a centre forward that the team was missing; given his characteristics and his interpretation of the game, his qualities were unquestionable. Just two years before coming to Milan, he’d played in the Champions League final, playing a key role in a competition with Borussia Dortmund.

“There are situations where, for a player, even a very important one, it matters how you feel. If you feel appreciated, valued, taken into consideration… When you play for a club like Milan, the weight of the shirt is completely different than when you play for other clubs.

“You feel it from the first day you join. I had no doubt that he could be what he’s demonstrating now.”.

“We tried to sign him back in June. We made a first attempt. In the final days of the transfer window, another important name we tried to sign was Akanji. The Champions League was crucial for both of them. They turned him down, not because of the club’s importance, but because he wasn’t playing in the Champions League.

“Then the opportunity arose again at the end of August for Rabiot. Defeat against Cremonese? No, we had already decided to bring him. It was just a matter of contract details.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It was difficult for us because we decided to change the formation five days before the transfer window closed. Switching from a 4-3-3 to a three-man defense meant we were having a really hard time finding a quality player in the last five days.

According to recent reports, “We were a bit unlucky, first with the Akanji story and then with Liverpool’s Joe Gomez… Guehi’s move from Crystal Palace to Liverpool fell through, and at the last minute they—we already had the deal ready, we were just waiting for this to happen—made a step back. And to avoid being left without a central defender at the last minute, we signed Odogu as a promising player.”.

On not being able to reach the Champions League and not being able to continue his work at Milan….

“This is the first time today, after all these months, that I’ve spoken about this… The wound of not reaching the Champions League is still enormous. I think that from the first day I arrived at Milan, even in the way I signed—I questioned myself with the type of contract.

“I said, ‘If I have to come only for the Champions League objective, then I don’t understand where I’ve come from.’ Milan has a different story. I had to go through a trial. The disappointment is that those who run the club didn’t understand how much time people needed, which is now being done, rightly so.

Recent findings suggest that “That is to say, it takes several transfer sessions to get a competitive team ready to win. At the beginning, I felt the responsibility to put the pieces together immediately, because after the defeat in the Coppa Italia final the year before, there were some important signs.

Industry observers note that “I didn’t know where to start. But I think we did an vital job last summer, we sold for a lot and also signed 10 newly introduced players. Then you need time to integrate, learn new philosophies and create a cohesive group, hungry to win.

Recent findings suggest that “Until March-April, we were a group with difficulties, but we were at the top of the table. Then in the last 10 matchdays, we had a mental breakdown, also due to other external dynamics, which I don’t want to discuss here, which had a significant impact.

“Internal or external dynamics? External to the team. But we also have some blame: myself first and foremost, along with Max [Allegri].

“We had to be a little more attentive to certain dynamics. We needed to be more present with the team to ultimately lead them to the final result. Isolation is the wrong word; I don’t believe in these things. I believe in teamwork; I believe in cohesion: from the club to the team.

“When this happens, you transmit it to the team. When these situations become possible, you could also see it in the team’s results, because the players are very attentive. Sometimes we think they have other interests, but they pay attention to everything that comes out. They follow everything very carefully and transmit it.

“Instilling serenity… How can you convey serenity? When, in difficult moments, you show that you believe in the project more than before. Sometimes I missed this feeling, a lack of something that could give us the final push.”.

According to recent reports, but despite this, did you think you could continue? Does this farewell after only a year feel like a stab in the back?

It has been revealed that “Look, I would have asked for a round table where we could all sit down together and analyze everything. Then they could have just said ‘no, thanks’… But I respect the decision they made. I accept it with great regret, but I’ve never questioned it because there’s someone above me who has to decide, including for the fate of the club.

“And when they decide to take a different path, you have to accept it. I know things could have gone differently, even much better. I’ll always be a Milan fan, even after an experience like that.”.

Was AC Milan a team that needed the constant presence of a manager or coach to avoid letting itself go as it later did?

Sources indicate that “The feeling I had at the beginning was that this leadership was a bit lacking. The arrival of Modric—and another of our goals was also Granit Xhaka, Leverkusen’s captain—was precisely to bring real players into the group, with crucial characteristics and capable of leading others.

Industry observers note that “Granit didn’t arrive; Luka arrived, who has a different way of being a leader: he does it in silence and with his attitude on the pitch. I had the opportunity to meet Mike Maignan: an extraordinary guy, a soul who cares deeply about the AC Milan shirt.

“Gabbia is another extraordinary guy; he lives for this club. Rabiot too… His experience spoke for itself. The great disappointment is that I expected something more in terms of responsibility and leadership from Pulisic: he’s a top-class player with unquestionable qualities. But in terms of performance, things happened that I had never experienced in my career….

Sources indicate that “Like Gimenez: an extraordinary guy with numbers that spoke for themselves; for a year he failed to score a goal. Then it happened that Pulisic didn’t score for six months. He scored a goal. Then Leao didn’t score for four months.

“Situations that are hard to come by in football have happened… It can happen that you don’t score for a month, two months, but that long a period of time also affected the team’s final performance.

Industry observers note that “Losing a match against Cagliari the way we did, 2-1, I think was the worst match of my life. The feeling and the disappointment I felt towards the fans in the stadium that night is something I will never forget for the rest of my life.”.

If Cardinale had been the Cardinale he is today, the one who is also physically present, would you still be AC ​​Milan’s DS?

Recent findings suggest that “I can’t answer that question; he has to answer it. I can say that I remember when the Jashari negotiations were going on… I had just landed in Rome and I was very pleased when he called me because he wanted to understand what was happening in that negotiation.

“I explained all the dynamics to him and I really liked that he said, ‘Anything you need, if you have to spend a little more, let me know because I’m here.’ Then during that process I never had the chance to talk to him, even intentionally.

It has been revealed that “There were other people above me who I never wanted to bypass. I never had a direct relationship with him, and the possibility of a discussion would have helped everyone. Not me, but everyone. By putting all the problems and dynamics on the table, we could have resolved things much sooner. But I think it’s a new experience for Cardinale.

Industry observers note that “He’s had experience in other sports in America. Now he’s done something crucial, taking responsibility and putting his face on the line. I would have preferred to have had that presence even when I was there because it would have been very useful. But for the Milan, better late than never.

“Now, for better or worse, he will make his own decisions and responsibilities. I think that for him, too, the best interests of Milan come first.”.

Was Leao a problem or a resource in your mind?

“I knew him from the outside. When I had the chance to meet him in person, I thought he was an extraordinary guy. I truly loved him as a person, like everyone else. But he was the player from whom we all expected something more. I think football was no longer a priority for him. That’s the key to understanding him.”.

“I think a bit about his life outside of football. Music, fashion, things… But I never doubted the sense of belonging he had towards Milan. You could sense that he loved playing for Milan and was suffering from not performing.
