Prince William led tributes for Harry Kane as Wembley honoured the England captain on reaching his record-breaking 126th cap against Croatia on Thursday.

Kane, who became the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or last month, celebrated another remarkable feat as he surpassed legendary goalkeeper Peter Shilton as England's most capped player in history.

After walking out with his four children for kick-off, followed by his England team-mates, the Bayern Munich forward first held his Ballon d'Or trophy aloft to Wembley's buoyant crowd, soaking up the celebrations.

Shilton approached the England captain to present him with a medal displaying his achievement, before Kane's former Spurs team-mate Luka Modric continued the tributes by offering him another gift.

Prince William then walked on to the pitch to shake Kane's hand and present him with a framed shirt, bearing the words 'Kane 126'.

As well as holding the record for England's most capped player, the 33-year-old striker is also England's highest ever scorer with 91 goals, ahead of Wayne Rooney and Sir Bobby Charlton who netted 53 and 49 respectively during their careers.

Prince William shakes Harry Kane's hand as he celebrates the England captain's record cap.

The Prince led tributes as Wembley honoured Kane ahead of England's clash with Croatia.

Kane, accompanied by his four children on the pitch, held his Ballon d'Or aloft to supporters.

Prince William applauded 'brilliant and remarkable' Kane on his Ballon d'Or triumph with a personal social media message after the ceremony in London.

It has been revealed that the Prince of Wales, signing his message off with his personal 'W' initial, posted on Instagram: 'Huge congratulations to Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or! What a fantastic achievement and so deserved.

'A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.'.

Kane, who has been widely regarded as a model professional and humble superstar during his career, admitted he still has an ego of sorts in an interview on the eve of his record-breaking England cap.

Asked if he has an ego, Kane replied: ‘That's a great question. I’m sure my wife will be able to say a thing or two!

'But ego is funny, because ego is many different things. I guess I have an ego to be the best, because I want to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’.

On becoming England's highest appearance maker, he joked that some of his current Three Lions team-mates might catch his total by the end of their careers.

‘Jude (Bellingham) and Declan (Rice), they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are,’ he added. ‘So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! The goal record is going to be the one that's difficult to beat. I think that’s good!

He has passed Peter Shilton as England's most capped player in history - with 126 to his name.

Kane receives a gift from ex-Spurs team-mate and fellow Ballon d'Or winner Luka Modric.

’In football, you’ve never completed it. No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has. This is no time to rest. If anything, I've got better year on year, and the numbers have got better.

In a recent development, 'While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I'm just on the back of scoring 73 goals in one year, which is incredible, and I want to get 100 England goals as quickly as possible.

Recent findings suggest that ‘My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I want to make sure that I cross every bridge and do everything possible so that, whenever that day comes, I can say, “I’ve done everything possible. I have this record, I don’t have this record, but it doesn’t matter, I can sleep well at night”.’.

Recent findings suggest that andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

Sources indicate that he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

In a recent development, when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson stated, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Recent findings suggest that any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Recent findings suggest that since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

Industry observers note that “He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola stated. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

In a recent development, don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Sources indicate that isak had an unusual afternoon. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

According to recent reports, “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose noted. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Sources indicate that andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

It has been revealed that there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has stated that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

Recent findings suggest that “We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Industry observers note that adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He mentioned: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

According to recent reports, he added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. According to recent reports, good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to latest heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, remarked: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

Sources indicate that the Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

Mauricio Pochettino could consider bringing Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun to Manchester United with him.

That is according to experienced former Tottenham, Everton and Aston Villa scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The 54-year-old's appointment was confirmed last week, with his first game in charge to come against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino was in charge of the United States for two years and guided them to a positive World Cup campaign in the summer, earning himself a new contract that he signed in August.

But the Argentine could not turn down Man United's offer down, and will return to the Premier League with a third team after stints at Tottenham and Chelsea.

His first transfer window will be a key one, with the Red Devils in the relegation zone and in need of major intervention.

McKennie and Balogun have been key parts of Pochettino's US team in the past two years.

The former is a key player for Juventus and has been capped 72 times by his country, appearing on both wings and in the centre of the pitch.

According to recent reports, balogun, on the other hand, declared for the US in 2023 and has scored 13 goals in 32 caps since. The 25-year-old came very close to signing for Everton on transfer deadline day and is expected to leave Monaco.

"I bet he wishes he could take Harry Kane," King told Football Insider when asked what Pochettino could take from his experience with Tottenham.

"Pochettino was obviously involved when Harry broke into the team. Manchester United, like Tottenham, need a centre-forward. There's no chance of Harry Kane going there, that is for sure.

"He's got a couple of options with the American players. He's got the boy McKennie at Juventus. He's got the lad who's at Monaco, Balogun.

It has been revealed that "He didn't win anything at Tottenham. He played decent football, but decent football doesn't wash at Manchester United. They've got to win cups.".

Speaking last week, Pochettino was asked about potentially signing players from his squad with the US.

Sources indicate that "Now is not the time [to talk about this]. All the good players always have dreams to reach the highest level," he noted. "And I think Manchester United is one of the teams that is in the highest level and it's the dream for many of the players.

"But now, I think they need to be focused on today, on tomorrow's game, on their clubs. I know really well for more than two years every single player. And I think they are all players with unbelievable talent.

"Of course, in the future, when that happens, of course we are going to pay attention, you know, to make some decisions and to pay attention to players that we know really well.".

Matteo Gabbia has admitted that he could return to the field in January for AC Milan, but he doesn’t want to rush back.

It has been a difficult season for Milan, at least where injuries are concerned. In defence, they have had issues reminiscent of the 2023/24 season, where Gabbia had to be brought back from his loan spell at Villarreal.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that this season, though, it seems Gerry Cardinale is going to go down a different route and spend to help Ruben Amorim with his defensive options. Indeed, there have been plenty of rumours about recruitments at the back.

However, Gabbia could again be a key returnee in January, with him hoping to return from injury early in the new year.

Speaking to Sky Sport (via MilanNews) – at an event organised by the Milan Foundation at Milan’s “Arturo Toscanini” secondary school, where they met with several children with disabilities – Gabbia discussed the importance of the event, as well as his recovery.

What were the emotions of this meeting?

Industry observers note that “It’s wonderful, very enjoyable to spend hours with them. It’s also beautiful to see how they manage to create a group, something that really demonstrates the importance of teamwork, the importance of friendship, even among themselves.

“We’re happy; we thank Fondazione Milan for the project, which is always beautiful and key: we’re happy to be a part of it and we’re enjoying the afternoon.”.

Are you able to rejoin the group in January?

According to recent reports, “Yes, that could be the time: we’re trying to work hard and do everything as best we can. I obviously have to thank the physiotherapists and the doctor because we’re really doing everything we can every day to try to heal the injury and get back on the pitch feeling good.

“It’s definitely been an unlucky season for me so far: I don’t want it to happen again or for any recurrences, so it’s also crucial to take the right time, get back in shape, and support the team right now.”.

In a recent development, “Although it’s bad for the team that there are so many injured players, we’re together right now, supporting each other and trying to encourage each other through therapy, gym work, and the entire recovery process. Therefore, we’re trying to work as a team this week too, to overcome all the players’ injuries.

“From a personal standpoint, I’m trying to take this time calmly, in the sense that these things are part of sport, part of life, and not all moments are the same.

“This is certainly a difficult time, but it still allows me to stay close to the team, to try to lend my support, even in the good and bad times. That’s what I’m doing, in addition to obviously doing what I can to try to return as soon as possible and make my contribution on the pitch.”.

How do you explain the team’s ups and downs?

“I think it’s something we need to get our heads around; we need to understand the importance of every game.

Sources indicate that “The other day I heard our coach give an interview in which he stated something crucial: we need to understand that every game, when you don’t win, is taken as a defeat, a heavy defeat. We need to truly understand the importance of every game and approach training to prepare 100%, as best as possible, for every match.

“Therefore, I think this is room for improvement, but I see a group that is really eager to improve, to work, and as a result, I’m sure we’ll be able to fix this flaw as well.

“Although we’ve had a good start to the year in the league and less so in the Europa League, we have plenty of time to improve and have a strong year.”.

  • It is just 16 days since Kane held his hands to his face, climbed up to the stage at the London Palladium and mentioned 'wow' when Ronaldo 'Il Fenomeno' presented him with the Ballon d'Or trophy that anointed him the best player in the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:17 EST, 12 November 2026.

Only giants have trodden the path that Harry Kane walked at Wembley on Thursday when he strode out on to the pitch on a bitterly cold winter night, his four young children by his side, and beheld the array of trophies, honours, adulation and respect that awaited him.

It is just 16 days since Kane held his hands to his face, climbed up to the stage at the London Palladium and mentioned 'wow' when Ronaldo 'Il Fenomeno' presented him with the Ballon d'Or trophy that anointed him the best player in the world.

Industry observers note that now, it sat before him on a plinth and Kane broke away from the England line-up and walked forward to hoist it aloft. He showed it to all the corners of the stadium and for a moment, it was framed against the giant tifo bearing his image and the words 'England's Finest' that towered over one end of the ground.

Industry observers note that but the Ballon d’Or is old news in the flood of honours that is coming Kane’s way in this golden summer of a great career. Kane had become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or for a quarter of a century and on Thursday night he was to break the 37-year-old record held by Peter Shilton for the most England caps. He scored the winner, too. Of course, he did.

It has been revealed that the occasion of England-Croatia in the Nations League was Kane's 126th appearance in an England shirt and Shilton stepped forward to hand him a small case containing a crest to mark the achievement. Finally, the Prince of Wales highlighted his appreciation to the England captain by presenting him with a commemorative shirt with 'Kane 126' emblazoned on it.

It was a night to feel the weight of football's history and the ghosts of greatness that people England's heritage. Kane belongs in the company he now keeps. He belongs in the pantheon of the game because he is one of the deadliest strikers in history. He belongs in the pantheon because of the humility he has shown and the dedication he devotes to improvement.

Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking England appearance with a finely struck penalty.

Before kick-off, Kane's history-making was celebrated with a commemorative shirt by the Prince of Wales.

England (4-2-3-1): Pickford 6; Alexander-Arnold 6 (White 78, 6), Quansah 4, Burn 6, Hall 7; Rice 5 (Garner 78, 5), Anderson 6; Rogers 8, Bellingham 6, Gordon 5 (Ngumoha 78, 5); Kane 7.

Goals: Rogers 24', Kane 64' (pen).

Croatia (4-2-3-1): Livakovic 5; Smolcic 6 (Marco Pasalic 76 5), Stanisic 6, Vuskovic 6, Gvardiol 5; Misic 5 (Modric 76, 6), Kovacic 6; Sucic 7 (Mario Pasalic 70, 5), Baturina 6, Vlasic 5; Matanovic 5 (Budimir 70, 5).

Recent findings suggest that he belongs with Billy Wright, the first England player to 100 caps, and the man who set the England appearance record at 105 when he played for his country for the last time in 1959. He belongs with Bobby Charlton, who made it to 106 before the heartbreak of the 1970 World Cup quarter-final defeat to West Germany brought his international career to an end.

Industry observers note that kane belongs with Bobby Moore, Charlton's rival as the greatest England player of all time, who reached the newly introduced mark of 108 caps in November 1973. That was one of the great numbers in English sport until Peter Shilton finally surpassed it. He reached 125 caps by the time he played his last game for England in the third-place play-off at the 1990 World Cup.

It has been revealed that it is quite some lineage. And now it is Kane who holds the prize. And if this was hardly a momentous match, it was a momentous occasion. If you are tired of glorying in a player like Kane, a relentless striker, a wonderful passer, the sweetest striker of the ball you will ever see, a player of vision, a man who exudes the beauty of simplicity and the wonder of modesty, then you are tired of football.

Sources indicate that the honours are rushing at him in a giddy, babbling flood. It may be that he reaches close to 200 caps before he retires and even if it already seems likely that that record will be broken by Jude Bellingham, who has 61 caps at the age of 23, Kane's England goals tally, which stands at 92 after another goal against Croatia, will not be under threat for a generation or longer.

Sources indicate that the gap, of course, is a tournament victory. That is what still separates Moore and Charlton from him. Kane is a dream of a player but he has not won the World Cup or the European Championship. What remains is the hope that he will put that right in the years that he has left in the game.

Winning the Nations League would not be quite the same but it would be a start and this victory over Croatia took England a small step closer to that goal. A convincing win over Spain in Madrid on Sunday would take them closer to their aim of finishing top of this group and getting a favourable draw in the quarter-finals in the spring.

Industry observers note that kane made his England debut in March 2015 when he was 21 and England's future looks brighter now than it did when he broke through. More than an hour before the game, the men who will follow Kane and perhaps even chase his caps record, chatted animatedly on the pitch. Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Gibbs-White are the latest breed.

Morgan Rogers opened the scoring inside the opening half-an-hour and celebrated with his trademark cold celebration.

England had found themselves pegged back by Croatia after slopping defending drew the visitors level.

Referee Morten Krogh was summoned to the monitor to review the penalty shout on Thursday.

Kane returned to Wembley triumphant for the first time since his historic Ballon d'Or win.

It has been revealed that after the Kane festivities, the first half was an anti-climax. Twenty-four minutes of relative drudgery ensued before Kane exhibited the breadth of his talent once again to help put England ahead. He got the ball 30 yards out, looked up and drifted a beautiful diagonal pass out to the right and into the path of Bellingham. Bellingham volleyed it across goal and Rogers forced it over the line.

Industry observers note that the second half began slowly, too, but 15 minutes into it, Croatia equalised. England failed to clear a corner, Jarell Quansah tried to head the ball back to Jordan Pickford and, as Kane watched on, Petar Sucic stole in and hooked the ball past the England goalkeeper into the roof of the net.

It has been revealed that quansah made some kind of amends three minutes later when he was dragged down in the box and Danish referee Morten Krogh awarded a penalty. It was Kane-time again. Kane took the kick and lifted it gently and with a touch of curl down the centre of the goal. Dominic Livakovic dived to his left and the ball sailed softly over his trailing leg and into the net.

Recent findings suggest that croatia had chances to draw level but could not take them. England made changes and young Rio Ngumoha, a winger of rare talent, another with a rich future ahead of him, another who will help to fill the void when the day comes for Kane to bid farewell to England, came on as a late substitute for Gordon.

Sources indicate that and so Kane's night of history began to draw to a close. In a 2-1 victory, he had made one and scored one. He remains as central to England's hopes of ending more than 60 years without a trophy as he ever has been. In a career that has festooned him with garlands and left no one in doubt of his greatness, it is the only gap that remains.

Harry Kane has set his sights firmly on rapidly reaching a century of international goals after becoming England’s most-capped player of all time.

The England skipper marked his 126th appearance for the Three Lions with the winner against Croatia in the Nations League – his first goal since picking up the Ballon d’Or last month.

Kane was afforded an emotional presentation pre-match at Wembley to mark both achievements and is already thinking of creating more history after moving within eight goals of a ton.

‘It’s achievable,’ Kane mentioned. ‘I’m getting closer. Breaking the appearance record is a massive thing in the history of our game, seeing the tifo at the stadium and having my kids with me was beyond dreams.

‘It’s important to recognise our great players. It’s maybe something we haven’t done so well over the years with some of our other greats.

‘It's been a crazy few weeks. I don’t know if I’ve fully taken it all in. The reception has been overwhelming.

‘Maybe during the winter break I’ll be on a beach reflecting on everything I’ve achieved, having a drink with my wife.’.

Croatia legend Luka Modric, 41, was part of the presentations ahead of kick off and Kane did not rule out attempting to prolong his career in a similar vein to the AC Milan midfielder.

Industry observers note that ‘He’s an inspiration for a lot of us,’ Kane added. ‘An incredible player and a great person, he’s looked after himself and still to be playing at this level is inspiring for me to push the limits. To see where your body and mentality takes you.

In a recent development, ‘As long as I feel I can help, I’ll be here for as long as I can. If that’s until I’m 40, we’ll wait and see.’.

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola said afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • After graduating from secondary school in Takayama City, he studied chemical engineering at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (now the Institute of Science Tokyo).
  • Chemistry education must change to help the planet: here’s how.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hideki Shirakawa pioneered the field of conductive polymers, overturning the common view that plastics do not conduct electricity. His demonstration that thin films of polyacetylene — an organic polymer — can become conductive when doped with small amounts of other chemicals earned him a share of the 2000 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (with Alan MacDiarmid and Alan Heeger). He was the second Japanese chemist to receive this award, after Kenichi Fukui in 1981. Shirakawa has died aged 90.

Shirakawa was born in Tokyo. After graduating from secondary school in Takayama City, he studied chemical engineering at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (now the Institute of Science Tokyo). He went on to pursue master’s and doctoral studies there, under the supervision of polymer chemist Shu Kambara, earning a Doctor of Engineering degree for his research on how blocks of organic molecules combine to form polymer chains.

Chemistry education must change to help the planet: here’s how.

Chemistry education must change to help the planet: here’s how.

According to recent reports, after completing his doctorate in 1966, Shirakawa was hired as a research associate in the laboratory of Sakuji Ikeda at Tokyo Tech. There, he began studying how acetylene molecules join together to form a polymer, using Ziegler–Natta catalysts (which are based on organic molecules containing transition metals).

In a recent development, in 1967, Shirakawa was joined in his experiments by a visiting researcher from South Korea, Hyung Chick Pyun. The pair were polymerizing acetylene using a catalyst composed of tetrabutoxytitanium and triethylaluminium to produce powdered polyacetylene.

On one occasion, however, the protocol failed to produce the powder. Instead, a ragged film formed on the surface of the solution in the flask. On closer inspection, it became clear that the visiting researcher had mistakenly used a much higher concentration of the catalyst than was intended — 1,000 times higher. Shirakawa went on to synthesize a thin film of polyacetylene with a metallic lustre by introducing acetylene gas into a flask coated on the inside with the concentrated catalyst.

Chemists struggle to ditch hazardous solvents — even after decades of ‘green’ efforts.

Chemists struggle to ditch hazardous solvents — even after decades of ‘green’ efforts.

Industry observers note that subsequently, he travelled to the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, where he worked with MacDiarmid and Heeger. The team discovered that adding small amounts of molecules that accept electrons (such as bromine) or that donate electrons (such as arsenic pentafluoride) increased the electrical conductivity of the thin film by a factor of ten million. This work led to the trio’s Nobel award.

In a recent development, as confirmed via premierleague.com, Sam Barrott will take charge of the match, with Adam Nunn and Lee Betts as his assistants, while Chris Kavanagh is fourth official. John Brooks is on VAR, assisted by Paul Howard.

The upcoming game is the Reds’ sixth home match in the top flight this season, and it’ll be the third to have had the Yorkshire native as the referee.

Upon learning that curious fact, Keith Hackett took to social media to endorse Barrott as a referee but question the decision-making process which has led to him being dispatched to Anfield once again.

The former chief executive of the PGMOL (now Pro Ref) posted on X: ‘A top-class referee, but not a very good appointing procedure by his bosses’.

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

It’s a strong show of faith by Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb to assign Barrott to what is always the most high-profile fixture in English football, and arguably world football.

Liverpool fans might be forgiven for not being able to summon much enthusiasm over the appointment, given the official’s previous at Anfield this season.

According to recent reports, in August, it was he who awarded Nottingham Forest a penalty in their 2-2 draw against the Reds when Neco Williams went to ground under a challenge from Alisson Becker. The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel subsequently adjudged that the spot kick was wrongly given.

While there are clear critera which must be observed when appointing match officials to specific fixtures – any officials from Merseyside or Manchester are obviously ineligible for Sunday’s clash at Anfield – seeing Barrott assigned to yet another Liverpool home game does seem anomalous.

We just hope – for his sake as much as anyone else’s – that the main talking point after the final whistle isn’t a controversial and decisive error on his part. The last thing we need is yet more dubious refereeeing affecting the Reds.

  • After Cummins’s remarkable press conference in Sydney on Friday morning, in which he called Khawaja’s various assertions ‘complete and utter nonsense’ and questioned the validity of their friendship, it was hard to discern any common ground, much less spot a middle way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LAWRENCE BOOTH, CRICKET CORRESPONDENT.

Published: 05:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 05:21 EST, 13 November 2026.

Pat Cummins is either the greatest actor in world sport – or the claim that the whole Australian team knew about the sandpaper plot in South Africa eight years ago is a figment of Usman Khawaja’s imagination.

After Cummins’s remarkable press conference in Sydney on Friday morning, in which he called Khawaja’s various assertions ‘complete and utter nonsense’ and questioned the validity of their friendship, it was hard to discern any common ground, much less spot a middle way.

According to the blue corner, everyone was in on the scam, sandpaper was used not just at Cape Town but in the previous Test at Port Elizabeth, and there was a team meeting to discuss the question of collective responsibility.

According to the red, those who knew about the plan did not include the bowlers, nothing untoward happened at Port Elizabeth, and there was no meeting.

The only thing that can be noted for certain after another tumultuous 24 hours for Australian cricket was that the two corners are now polar opposites, each eyeing the other with suspicion and incredulity. Barring an improbable climbdown, the twain can never meet.

It has been revealed that cummins, it must be said, eased into his work after an emotional start behind a lectern at the Cricket Central venue in Sydney’s Olympic Park. He began by stating his basic position, then invited questions, which for the next hour and a bit he handled with aplomb and a degree of statesmanship.

Pat Cummins held a remarkable press conference in Sydney to address the sandpaper claims.

Speaking for more than an hour, Cummins dismissed Khawaja’s various assertions as ‘complete and utter nonsense’ and questioned the validity of their friendship.

This will not please those who still find it impossible to believe that Cummins and his fellow seamers on that trip, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, knew nothing of the scheme that led to bans for three batsmen – Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.

After all, as any bowler will tell you, the idea that the condition of their most prized possession might be altered without their noticing is as absurd as trying to persuade a batsman to walk out without his favourite willow.

And yet. Cummins stuck to his guns, in contrast to Khawaja’s appearance on the ABC on Wednesday evening, when he repeatedly declined to name Cummins as one of the guilty party. And while Khawaja reacted to his TV grilling by cancelling media engagements, Cummins made it clear he would be answering every question that came his way.

Whichever side you believe, and whatever the doubts that remain, his press conference grabbed the momentum from Team Khawaja.

Sources indicate that it also made the previous day’s appearance by Mitchell Marsh, Australia’s white-ball captain for the next three weeks against England, all the more bizarre. By refusing to engage with any of the questions raised by Khawaja’s autobiography, Marsh – himself a veteran of South Africa 2018 – did little to dispel the suspicion that Khawaja had a point.

And that in turn encouraged the view that Cummins, who called his own press conference without the knowledge of Cricket Australia, might be about to come clean.

Instead, he doubled down on the denial he and his bowling colleagues had issued in 2021, but now went further, taking a clear-eyed and devastating aim at Khawaja’s integrity.

‘Usman is a friend, but friends aren’t casual with each other’s lives and reputations,’ said Cummins. ‘He’s dealt with the way he’s presented his story in a very casual manner and it affects a lot of people. That’s what I’m grappling with at the moment, because I don’t think that’s OK. It’s not what friends do.’.

Cummins plainly intended this to be his final word on the matter, but the problem facing Australian cricket is that the sore may never properly heal.

David Warner then hit back at Cummins and accused him of 'throwing Khawaja under the bus'.

Only a couple of hours after Cummins finished, Warner – at Perth’s Optus Stadium as a TV pundit for the first ODI between Australia and England – was being asked for his view, and he didn’t hold back, repeating his belief that Khawaja’s version of events was ‘the truth’.

It has been revealed that he added: ‘I really, really support him. I actually feel for him at the moment. I feel that the captain today threw Uzzy under the bus and I’m very, very disappointed about that.’.

Disappointment. It’s mutual, and it’s everywhere. Cummins provided a brief distraction, but it doesn’t change the fact that this is a civil war with no obvious resolution.

Offered the chance to kick Australian cricket while it was down, England made humiliating contact with fresh air on the opening day of their eight-match white-ball trip.

Only hours after Pat Cummins had added a twist to the sandpaper saga by dismissing Usman Khawaja’s claims that the whole squad knew about the ball-tampering plans in South Africa eight years ago as ‘complete and utter nonsense’, Harry Brook’s side were blown away for 131 in the first ODI – having at one stage been 65 for eight.

Australia then romped home by seven wickets with more than 26 overs in hand to take a 1–0 lead into the second game of this three-match series in Adelaide on Sunday. For England, anyway, complete and utter nonsense felt about right.

It is not quite a year since they began their Ashes campaign here at the Optus Stadium by being bowled out in 32.5 overs in their first innings and 34.4 in their second – before stumbling to a 4–1 defeat.

Now, they obligingly split the difference, dismissed in 33.4 as Mahli Beardman, a 21-year-old fast bowler from Dunsborough, a couple of hours drive down the coast from Perth, picked up six for 34 – the best figures for Australia by an ODI debutant.

His first victim was Joe Root, caught behind for a painful 17 off 36 balls, and his second Brook, who had made only a single when he fidgeted fatally outside off stump.

According to recent reports, that might have been enough to satisfy most newcomers, but Beardman had barely started. Jordan Cox made two before edging a poke, and Sam Curran top-edged a pull to fine leg for a duck.

When Liam Dawson, yet to score, squeezed a drive to backward point, Beardman had five wickets in 28 balls – not bad for a player whose only previous taste of international cricket had come in a T20 in Pakistan in January.

He then ended a lively last-wicket stand of 29 by removing Jofra Archer, who had just driven him down the ground for four. It was the only authentic boundary England managed off his bowling: the other, a streaky inside edge from Root, summed up the problems posed by his pace, bounce and accuracy. As bids for a place on next summer’s Ashes tour go, this was hard to ignore.

Industry observers note that ‘Laying in bed last night, that’s not what I had planned,’ noted Beardman, who was taken under his wing by Australian fast-bowling legend Dennis Lillee after a mutual friend spotted him as a young teenager bowling at a bin down the side of a house. ‘It was an incredible game and it all happened so fast.’.

If England had learned lessons from their collapses in the last year’s Test here, they demonstrated little sign of being able to implement them. Players drove on the up, as they had so heedlessly a year earlier, and failed to cope with the Perth bounce.

England head coach Brendon McCullum was critical of his side's failure to adapt to the pitch, and called on them to learn from their mistakes going forward.

Recent findings suggest that 'It’s a bit like batting on a trampoline,' stated McCullum. 'There are certain shots that are very difficult to execute. We talked about trying to put those away. We probably knew we were in for a low-scoring contest, but we expected to get a few more runs than 130.

Industry observers note that 'We're disappointed but there are some good lessons for us. If you look towards the World Cup in South Africa there’s going to be some pitches there that will test us from a bounce point of view.'.

And all this after they had played a warm-up game at the WACA – a grievous omission before the Ashes – and trained with such intensity that white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen had declared it the best practice session he had seen from an England team.

In the event, their top-scorer was Gus Atkinson, who hit an unbeaten 29 from No 10, including England’s only six.

Mitchell Marsh, stroke-less in the previous day’s press conference, put that into perspective by clearing the ropes four times during a 29-ball half-century, while Cooper Connolly – dropped by Tom Banton at midwicket on five – hit two sixes himself.

England’s only consolation had come at the start of Australia’s reply, when Atkinson bowled Travis Head first ball off the inside edge. Head it was who had taken care of Australia’s fourth-innings chase here a year ago, thrashing a 69-ball century that knocked the stuffing out of Ben Stokes’s attack.

According to recent reports, instead, it was Marsh who went for his shots, stopped only when he flicked Jamie Overton to Ben Duckett at deep midwicket, by which time Australia were already halfway there. For a few hours, at least, no one was talking about sandpaper.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikey Moore must be brought back to Tottenham Hotspur in January after an unsuccessful loan move to FC Koln.

That is the opinion of former senior Tottenham scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The 19-year-old has not scored a single goal or provided an assist in nine appearances for the German side so far this season, and appears to be struggling to adapt.

It has been revealed that it was not clear whether Moore would be loaned out at all this season. He enjoyed a strong pre-season with Tottenham and scored and assisted against Charlton in the Carabao Cup in August.

The winger spent last season with Rangers and seemed to thrive off the experience, with many believing him ready to make an impact in Roberto De Zerbi's team.

Ultimately, however, the arrivals of Savinho, Mykhailo Mudryk and Omar Marmoush made a loan likely the more beneficial decision for Moore.

Tottenham's relief will be that Moore is, at least, getting the minutes he needs at Koln - the winger has appeared in every game since he arrived, starting six of nine.

And the Lilywhites will hope that if the team's form improves over the coming months, so will the winger's.

Koln have won just one game in the Bundesliga since Moore arrived, scoring just seven goals and at the moment sitting 15th.

It has been revealed that "Now, that is a disappointment, isn't it? Wrong place to go on loan for me," King told Football Insider. "Again, that's Tottenham.

According to recent reports, "They got rid of the boy [Will] Lankshear, and now this kid's gone to Germany. It's one thing going to Glasgow Rangers. At least you haven't got a problem with the language.

"He had a decent start to the season at Tottenham. For me, it was the wrong club. He'd have done far better staying, okay, he might not have been playing in the first team, but then you don't know.

"I would have been happier for him to be working and training with the first team at Tottenham, and maybe looking for a Championship club.

"He's had five starts at Koln. I would say the writings on the wall. January, come home, son.".

Moore started and scored for England's Under-21s on Monday as they beat France 3-2.

Sources indicate that speaking after the game, he was asked about his season and said: "Obviously it’s not been an easy start. It’s been a tough run of results, a tough start for us as a team.

"I think I’m doing quite well with my performances but I’ve got a lot more to add with goals and assists because that’s what everyone looks at.

"For me personally, that’s what I need to add and then as a team we need to climb the table because we don’t want to be so close to that relegation zone.”.

"I think he has to continue in that same place he's been since the start of the season," Iraola said earlier this month.

"We trust him, he's doing very well, he needs to continue, we have to encourage him.”.

Industry News: Why Man United staff feel treatment of Michael Carrick was 'disgusting' and the comment from Omar Berrada that raised eyebrows as club legend is put out of his misery - and Mauricio Pochettino gets set to take over

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1051 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 14:25 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:15 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino would have been fast asleep in his hotel room in the quirky American town of Trilith when Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sat down with Michael Carrick at Carrington Thursday morning and confirmed the worst-kept secret in football.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:25 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:15 EST, 13 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino would have been fast asleep in his hotel room in the quirky American town of Trilith when Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sat down with Michael Carrick at Carrington Thursday morning and confirmed the worst-kept secret in football.

It was time for Carrick to vacate the head coach’s office at Manchester United, and safe to say Pochettino will have his feet under the desk this time next week.

Carrick arrived at 7.50am but, unlike the last two days, he was no longer wearing his United training gear.

The agonising wait to be put out of his misery was over, and the club’s chief executive and director of football duly administered the last rites before Carrick left at 10.18am.

The decision was communicated to staff and Under-21s boss Adam Lawrence took training with the players who have remained at Carrington during the international break.

The first reports of Carrick’s sacking broke at 9.30am, but United insisted that they were premature and it wasn’t until 10.37am that the news was confirmed in a 142-word statement.

Michael Carrick finally left Carrington on Thursday morning after an agonising wait to be put out of his misery.

Staff at Manchester United believe that the former club captain's treatment at the hands of their Ineos paymasters has been 'disgusting'.

Industry observers note that it's understood that his backroom staff - assistant Steve Holland, coaches Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, and goalkeeper coach Craig Mawson - have also gone. When Evans left on Wednesday night with his car piled high with cardboard boxes, it didn't bode well.

The treatment of Carrick and Evans, in particular, has upset staff. Two highly-respected figures at United, whose association with the club goes back more than 20 years, have been left hanging while their employers stumble over a succession plan.

Members of staff share Gary Neville’s view that Berrada and Wilcox meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco, and making a move for Pochettino while Carrick had to keep driving past the cameras on his way into Carrington for the last three days, was ‘disgusting’.

It has also reignited anger over the 450 job cuts carried out by Ratcliffe and Ineos over the past three years while pouring millions down the drain in compensation.

The £10million to buy Pochettino and his staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation, and the pay-off owing to Carrick and Co, will push the cost of hiring and firing coaches in the Ineos era close to £50m.

No wonder eyebrows were raised when Berrada spoke at Sir Alex Ferguson’s 40th anniversary dinner at Old Trafford on Friday night and talked about building a culture at the club.

The feeling is that changing United’s head coach won’t make a shred of difference if there isn’t significant change higher up the chain.

It has once again turned the spotlight on the relationship between Ratcliffe and the Glazer family, who from February can force him to sell his 28 per cent holding to a third party for less than the £25-per-share he paid in 2024 unless he can match the offer and buy the club himself.

However, United sources say they had little choice but to sack Carrick with the club in the relegation zone, having decided to give him a stay of execution at the end of last month.

Since then, the club had carried out a comprehensive review and come to the conclusion that a record of one win from 10 Premier League games was unacceptable.

The sources indicated that the United board shared the frustration and anger felt by fans over the situation, and believe that a change of head coach will bring about an improvement from a squad that is far better than results would suggest.

While United praised Carrick for his ‘highest degree of professionalism’, there was only silence from the players on social media.

Many of them are on international duty, including Bruno Fernandes whose criticism of Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat to Como proved so damaging.

Following the announcement of Carrick's dismissal none of his former players - including Bruno Fernandes - were quick to say their goodbyes publicly.

Meanwhile, his would-be successor Mauricio Pochettino is set to face the media on Friday.

Pochettino will inherit this squad of players once he has completed his duties as US national team coach with the upcoming CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is due to speak at 2.15pm Friday ahead of the first leg in Miami on Saturday night when he will face questions over the United job for the first time.

Pochettino is expected to stay in charge for the second leg in Cincinnati in the early hours of Wednesday morning before flying to Manchester to meet the players and prepare for the crunch clash with Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

The US have been staying in Trilith, near their fresh training headquarters in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta, where they were also based before the World Cup.

Sources indicate that it’s a unique place designed for the film industry and built around the Trilith Studios which are the largest outside Hollywood. The ideal place for Pochettino to prepare for life at Old Trafford.

He has embraced the American lifestyle since he was appointed US coach in September 2024, a few months after leaving Chelsea, and will be sorry to leave.

Pochettino is remarked to have developed a love of bourbon whiskey, country music and Nashville, with Ella Langley’s Choosin’ Texas one of his favourite tunes.

He has admitted crying over Miracle, the movie about the US hockey team made up of college kids famously beating the Soviet Union to the gold medal at the 1980 Winter Olympics.

But the pull of Manchester United was always going to be too great, and very soon he will be swapping Trilith for Old Trafford.
